chunks: As for what al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

Three things come out from the urethra: manī, and in it there is ghusl; and wady, from which there is wudu, because it comes from the dribbling of urine. He said: and madhy, there is no wudu in it; rather, it is like what comes out from the nose.

His statement عليه السلام, 'and wady, from which there is wudu,' is to be understood as meaning that if he had not performed istibrāʾ from urine as we mentioned, and then something came out from him after that, repeating wudu becomes obligatory upon him, because it would be from the remainder of urine. He alerted to that by his statement, 'because it comes from the dribbling of urine,' indicating that this is either urine or mixed with urine. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned...

key_terms.اسْتَبْرَأَ: performed cleansing precaution to ensure no urine remains
key_terms.الْإِحْلِيلِ: the urethral outlet from which the mentioned fluids emerge
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required after the emission of manī
key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: pre-seminal fluid that does not require wudu here
key_terms.الْوَدْيُ: a discharge associated here with urine residue and requiring wudu in that context
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: ritual ablution required for prayer and affected by certain discharges
key_terms.دَرِيرَةِ الْبَوْلِ: the dribbling or trace-flow of urine

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on madhy and wady in relation to wudu and ghusl in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal rulings of fluids exiting from the male organ and their effect on ritual purity. It distinguishes between manī, which necessitates ghusl, and madhy, which does not invalidate wudu, while explaining that wady requires wudu when it is connected to remaining urine.
